meta.title: storytelling — a daily interview that slowly turns into you
meta.description: An open-source, local-first AI that listens to your voice memos, transcribes them, and quietly writes a literary autobiography in plain Markdown — one short recording at a time.

hero.body: storytelling is a local-first AI that listens to your voice memos, transcribes them, and quietly writes them into a literary autobiography — one short recording at a time. It lives in a folder on your own disk, in plain Markdown. No cloud lock-in. No terms of service over your memories.

loop.body: storytelling runs as agent skills on your own machine. Each one does a single small thing; together they form a loop — every answer you record makes tomorrow's question a little sharper.

steps.name: Listen
steps.desc: Pulls new recordings out of Apple Voice Memos — audio, title, date — and files each one into its own self-contained folder.

steps.name: Transcribe
steps.desc: Turns the audio into plain-text transcripts, with your personal hotword list so names, places and projects come out right.

steps.name: Write
steps.desc: Reads the transcripts and writes your biography — in a literary voice you define. By default: Murakami-esque. Restrained, precise, a little sad.

steps.name: Interview
steps.desc: Reads the biography, finds the gaps, and asks the one question only it could ask today. Then you answer — and the loop starts over.

manuscript.body: Everything lives under ~/.storytelling as plain Markdown with YAML frontmatter — the same format your notes and wikis use. Years become volumes, months become chapters, every piece of writing a section. Grep it, version it with git, print it into a book, or hand it to any AI as memory.

principles.eyebrow: what this is, in three lines

items.title: Voice in, Markdown out.
items.body: Every recording ends as a typed, timestamped, source-annotated Markdown file on your disk. Nothing is locked inside a SaaS.

items.title: Local-first, forever.
items.body: Your autobiography sits in a folder you control. Move it, back it up, version it, hand it to another agent — it never stops being yours.

items.title: The interviewer gets better at asking.
items.body: Today's question is shaped by everything you've said before. The loop is the product.

footer.lineA: The first ten days are mine.
